subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a core shell-facing admin notification broadcast now, fold it into broader Control UI notification architecture, or leave shell alerts to plugin/external paths?
rationale: The feature is absent and plausible, but it creates a new admin-controlled UI interruption path that affects Gateway authorization, payload policy, Control UI UX, and plugin/core boundaries.

options.title: Design core notify contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical shell/admin notification request and require an explicit Gateway event/RPC, CLI, UI, and security contract before implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader UI notifications
options.body: Make the broader Control UI notification-system tracker own the shared toast/action architecture, but keep this issue linked until shell/admin broadcast is explicitly covered.

options.title: Prefer plugin or external delivery
options.body: Reject a core command and document the supported plugin, Web Push, node notification, or external alerting path if maintainers do not want shell scripts to interrupt Control UI sessions directly.

recommendation.title: Design core notify contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical shell/admin notification request and require an explicit Gateway event/RPC, CLI, UI, and security contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest routing candidate from Gateway broadcast, CLI surface, and prior product/security review history.
